subject: math
cluster: Work with radicals and integer exponents
intro: These problems mix large and small magnitudes, chain an estimate with a comparison, and ask you to judge whether a magnitude claim is reasonable. Watch your signs when subtracting a negative exponent, and always re-express your final answer as a single digit times an integer power of 10.

items.prompt: Quantity A is $6 \times 10^{5}$ and quantity B is $3 \times 10^{-2}$. How many times as large as B is A? Give your answer in single-digit-times-power-of-10 form.

steps: Subtract the exponents, being careful with the negative: $5 - (-2) = 5 + 2 = 7$.
So A is $2 \times 10^{7}$ times as large as B.

items.prompt: A grain of sand has a mass of about $4 \times 10^{-3}$ g. A boulder has a mass of about $8 \times 10^{6}$ g. About how many times as massive as the grain of sand is the boulder? Write the answer in single-digit-times-power-of-10 form.

steps: The boulder is about $2 \times 10^{9}$ times as massive as the grain of sand.

items.prompt: The diameter of a human hair is about $9 \times 10^{-5}$ m and the diameter of a virus is about $3 \times 10^{-8}$ m. How many times as wide as the virus is the hair? Express the answer in single-digit-times-power-of-10 form.

steps: The hair is $3 \times 10^{3}$ times as wide as the virus, or about $3000$ times.

items.prompt: A factory makes about $5 \times 10^{4}$ widgets each day, and each widget weighs about $4 \times 10^{-1}$ kg. Estimate the total mass of one day's widgets in single-digit-times-power-of-10 form.

steps: This gives $20 \times 10^{3}$, which is not single-digit form, so renormalize: $20 \times 10^{3} = 2 \times 10^{1} \times 10^{3} = 2 \times 10^{4}$.
The total mass is about $2 \times 10^{4}$ kg.

items.prompt: A city of about $8 \times 10^{5}$ people each generates about $5 \times 10^{-1}$ kg of recyclable plastic per day. Estimate the city's total daily recyclable plastic in single-digit-times-power-of-10 form.

steps: The city generates about $4 \times 10^{5}$ kg of recyclable plastic per day.

items.prompt: Light travels about $3 \times 10^{8}$ m in one second. A certain signal lasts only $2 \times 10^{-3}$ s. Estimate how far light travels during that signal, in single-digit-times-power-of-10 form.

steps: Distance = speed $\times$ time, so multiply the leading digits: $3 \times 2 = 6$.
Light travels about $6 \times 10^{5}$ m during the signal.

items.prompt: A student claims that a quantity of $7 \times 10^{6}$ is about $100$ times as large as a quantity of $7 \times 10^{3}$. Is the claim reasonable? Justify your answer using the exponents.
items.answer: No; it is about $1000$ times as large, not $100$.

steps: The exponent difference of $3$ means it is about $10^{3} = 1000$ times as large, not $10^{2} = 100$. The claim is not reasonable.
solution.answer: No; it is about $1000$ times as large, not $100$.

items.prompt: A scientist measures a quantity as $0.00000064$ and wants to write it as a single digit times an integer power of 10 (rounding the leading factor to one digit). Write the result.

steps: Write the number in single-digit-times-power-of-10 form: $0.00000064 = 6.4 \times 10^{-7}$ (the first nonzero digit is in the seventh place after the decimal point).
Round the leading factor $6.4$ to one digit: $6.4$ rounds to $6$.
The exponent is negative because the number is less than $1$.

items.prompt: Quantity P is $1 \times 10^{8}$ and quantity Q is $4 \times 10^{2}$. How many times as large as Q is P? Express the answer in single-digit-times-power-of-10 form.

steps: This gives $0.25 \times 10^{6}$, which is not single-digit form, so renormalize: $0.25 \times 10^{6} = 2.5 \times 10^{-1} \times 10^{6} = 2.5 \times 10^{5}$.
P is $2.5 \times 10^{5}$ times as large as Q, or $250{,}000$ times.

items.prompt: The mass of Earth is about $6 \times 10^{24}$ kg and the mass of a dust particle is about $2 \times 10^{-9}$ kg. How many times as massive as the dust particle is Earth? Write the answer in single-digit-times-power-of-10 form.

steps: Earth is about $3 \times 10^{33}$ times as massive as the dust particle.

items.prompt: An online video service streams about $9 \times 10^{9}$ minutes of video per day. Each minute uses about $5 \times 10^{-2}$ gigabytes of data. Estimate the total data streamed per day in single-digit-times-power-of-10 form.

steps: The service streams about $4.5 \times 10^{8}$ gigabytes per day.

items.prompt: A blogger writes that the national debt of about $3 \times 10^{13}$ dollars works out to about $1 \times 10^{4}$ dollars per person for a population of about $3 \times 10^{8}$ people. Use exponents to check whether $1 \times 10^{4}$ is a reasonable per-person amount.
items.answer: No; it is about $1 \times 10^{5}$ dollars per person, not $1 \times 10^{4}$.

steps: Divide the total debt by the population: $\frac{3 \times 10^{13}}{3 \times 10^{8}}$.
So the amount per person is $1 \times 10^{5} = 100{,}000$ dollars, not $1 \times 10^{4}$. The blogger's figure is off by one power of 10, so the claim is not reasonable.
solution.answer: No; it is about $1 \times 10^{5}$ dollars per person, not $1 \times 10^{4}$.

items.prompt: A reservoir holds about $8 \times 10^{6}$ liters of water. A leak drains it at about $4 \times 10^{-1}$ liter per second. Estimate how many seconds it takes to drain the reservoir, in single-digit-times-power-of-10 form.

An atom is about $1 \times 10^{-10}$ m across and a marble is about $2 \times 10^{-2}$ m across. How many times as wide as the atom is the marble? Write the answer in single-digit-times-power-of-10 form.

steps: The marble is about $2 \times 10^{8}$ times as wide as the atom.

items.prompt: Galaxy A contains about $4 \times 10^{11}$ stars. Galaxy B contains about $8 \times 10^{8}$ stars. First estimate how many times as many stars Galaxy A has as Galaxy B, then state how many powers of 10 apart they are (to the nearest whole power). Give the times-as-many value in single-digit-times-power-of-10 form.

steps: So Galaxy A has about $5 \times 10^{2}$ times as many stars. Since $5 \times 10^{2}$ is between $10^{2}$ and $10^{3}$ and is closer to $10^{3}$ ($500$ vs $100$ and $1000$), they are about $3$ powers of 10 apart.
